1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which derives the user solely from the HttpOnly session cookie (sessions.get(id) -> session.userId), never from a request-supplied identifier.

2.why: Codes are bound to the owning session/user (data.code === auth.session.identityCode, phone must match auth.user.phone, TOTP checked against that user's own encrypted secret), so a code does not work for other users.

3.why: Neither /api/mfa/activate nor /api/mfa/regenerate-backups deletes other sessions in the sessions Map, so any prior sessions for the user remain valid until idle/absolute timeout or explicit logout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encrypt() -> encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes (makeBackups), never in plaintext.

5.why: All secrets, session ids, identity codes, and recovery codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The client uses no localStorage/sessionStorage (only in-memory JS variables) and the sole cookie mfa_session is set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: All server-side inputs are strictly validated with allow-list regexes (validEmail, validPhone, validOTP, validRecovery, validCSRF, manualSecret pattern) and rejected otherwise; there are no SQL queries to inject.

8.why: Every dynamic value interpolated into innerHTML (message, secret, provisioningUri, testOtp, backup codes, logs) passes through the esc() HTML-encoder, backed by a strict nonce-based CSP.

9.why: The only redirect in the system is the fixed HTTP->HTTPS 308 to https://localhost:3000/, with no user-controllable redirect target anywhere.

10.why: secureHeaders sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', plus a stricter nonce-based CSP on the HTML page.

11.why: cookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes, and clearedCookie() mirrors them on logout.

12.why: The server never logs and returns only generic errors, but the client log() function writes the identity code, current OTP, and full backup codes to console.log and a visible logs panel, so codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code expires after 5 minutes, is marked identityUsed and cleared on success, and TOTP replay within a window is blocked via verifiedCounter !== count.

14.why: fail() locks identity, TOTP, and recovery verification for 5 minutes after 5 failures, with 429 responses while locked.

15.why: A fresh session id is issued on signin and rotated again after identity verification (sessions.delete + createSession), with 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts and server-side invalidation plus cookie clearing on logout.
